title: Tic-Tac-Toe Winner (N x N, K in a row)
statement:
You are writing the referee for a tic-tac-toe game server. The board is n x n, and a player wins by getting k of their marks in consecutive cells along a row, a column or a diagonal (either direction). A run longer than k also wins. Marks with a gap between them do not form a line.

Write def solution(n, k, moves). moves is a list of [row, col] cells (0-indexed). Players alternate: the first move is X, the second O, and so on. Every move is on the board and on an empty cell.

Replay the moves in order. Return "X" or "O" for the first player to complete k in a row (ignore any moves after that). If nobody wins and all n * n cells are filled, return "Draw". Otherwise return "Pending".

examples.why: X plays (0,0), (0,1), (0,2): the whole top row.
All 9 cells are filled and no line of 3 belongs to one player.
Two moves on a 16-cell board: the game is still going.

constraints: every move is a distinct [row, col] with 0 ≤ row, col < n

think.a: Replay moves in order. X plays on even indexes (0, 2, 4...), O on odd ones. The first time a player has k marks in a straight line, the game ends and that player wins. If moves run out first: full board means "Draw", anything else means "Pending".
After move 5, row 0 is X X X. Three in a row for X, so return "X". Before that move no line had 3.

think.q: What is the first thing you would write?
think.a: After every move, scan every cell and every direction for k in a row. That is O(n^2 · k) per move and O(n^4 · k) for a whole game. On a 150 x 150 board that is billions of steps.

"replay moves", "first player to..." → simulation. The key observation: a new winning line must pass through the cell just played. Every other line was already checked. So check only the 4 lines through the last move, counting matching marks in both directions.

1. Make an empty n x n board.
  2. For move i: mark = X if i is even, else O. Place it.
  3. For each direction (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), (1,-1): walk forward and backward while the cells match, count them, add 1 for the cell itself.
  4. If any count ≥ k, return the mark.
  5. After the loop: "Draw" if len(moves) == n * n, else "Pending".

No moves. n = 1, k = 1 (the first move wins). The winning move also fills the board (a win, not a draw). Moves after the win. The last move lands in the middle of a line (X _ X, then X fills the gap). Anti-diagonals, which are easy to forget. k < n, so a line does not have to touch the edge.

hints: You never need to rescan the whole board. Which lines can a single new mark complete?
Use four direction vectors: (0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1), (1, -1). For each one, count matching cells going +d and going -d, then add 1.
Check the win before deciding Draw: a move can fill the last cell and complete a line at the same time.
solution:
DIRS = [(0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1), (1, -1)]   # row, column, diagonal, anti-diagonal

def count(board, n, r, c, dr, dc, mark):
    # how many cells in a row match `mark`, walking from (r, c) one way
    k = 0
    r, c = r + dr, c + dc
    while 0 <= r < n and 0 <= c < n and board[r][c] == mark:
        k += 1
        r, c = r + dr, c + dc
    return k

def solution(n, k, moves):
    board = [[None] * n for _ in range(n)]
    for i, (r, c) in enumerate(moves):
        mark = 'X' if i % 2 == 0 else 'O'
        board[r][c] = mark
        # Only a line through the move just played can be new, so check
        # the 4 lines through (r, c) and count both ways along each.
        for dr, dc in DIRS:
            line = 1 + count(board, n, r, c, dr, dc, mark) + count(board, n, r, c, -dr, -dc, mark)
            if line >= k:
                return mark
    return 'Draw' if len(moves) == n * n else 'Pending'
explain:
Each move can only create lines that pass through its own cell. So after placing a mark at (r, c), look along 4 directions. For each, walk outward both ways while the marks match.

  • Example 1, move 5: X at (0, 2). Direction (0, 1): forward goes off the board (0), backward finds X at (0, 1) and (0, 0) (2). Line = 1 + 0 + 2 = 3 ≥ 3, so X wins.
  • Example 2: after each of the 9 moves the longest line through the new mark is 2, so nobody wins, and 9 moves = 3 x 3 cells means "Draw".

Each check walks at most k - 1 cells each way before a mismatch or the edge stops it (you can also cap it at k), so one move costs O(k) instead of O(n^2 · k). In a take-home, this check lives in a Board.place(r, c) method so the HTTP layer only asks "who won?".
complexity: O(len(moves) * k) time, O(n^2) space for the board

tests.label: 1 x 1 board
tests.why: the first move is already k = 1 in a row

tests.label: win on the last cell
tests.why: the 9th move fills the board and completes the diagonal: a win, not a draw

tests.label: moves after the win
tests.why: O also completes a row later, but X won first

tests.label: gap filled in the middle
tests.why: X _ X becomes X X X when X fills the gap: count both ways from the new cell

tests.label: marks with gaps are not a line
tests.why: X holds (0,0), (0,2), (0,4): three in the same row, but not consecutive

tests.label: run longer than k
tests.why: X has XX_XX in row 0 (no 3 yet); filling the gap makes a run of 5, which is at least k = 3

tests.label: k smaller than n, diagonal
tests.why: four in a row on the main diagonal, not touching a corner

tests.label: k = n blocked diagonal
tests.why: X has 3 on the diagonal but O took (3,3)

govtech.evidence: Tic-tac-toe appears among the GovTech take-homes found in public candidate repos; the original brief is not reproduced here, and the n x n, k-in-a-row version and the return values are ours.
extensions: Validate moves instead of trusting them: out of bounds, cell already taken, wrong player's turn, or a move after the game ended. Return a clear error for each.
Make it multiplayer over HTTP: POST /games, POST /games/{id}/moves, GET /games/{id}. How do you stop two requests for the same game from both placing a move? (A version number or a per-game lock.)
Support 3 or more players with their own marks. What changes? Only how you pick the mark for move i: players[i % len(players)].
Detect an early draw: return "Draw" as soon as no line of k can still be completed by anyone, not only when the board is full.
The board is 10^9 x 10^9 (infinite tic-tac-toe). Store only played cells in a dict keyed by (r, c); the O(k) check still works.
